# 4.2 · Bigram Language Model

`Level 4: Language From Scratch` · `+25 XP` · `drill 2 of 3`

## The job
Build the smallest real language model. `BigramLM.fit(sentences)` counts which token follows
which, wrapping each sentence in `<s>` and `</s>`. `prob(prev, word)` uses add-alpha
smoothing over the vocabulary (every token seen in training, plus `</s>`).
`perplexity(sentence)` scores how surprised the model is. `generate(rng, max_len)` samples
tokens until it draws `</s>` or reaches `max_len`.

## Why it matters
Perplexity is still the headline number in language model papers, and "predict the next
token, then sample" is exactly how chat models write. Smoothing teaches the oldest lesson
in the field: a model that assigns zero probability to anything it has not seen will fail
on the first new sentence it meets.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 4.2     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 4.2      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Store counts as `counts[prev][next]` with a `defaultdict(Counter)`.
2. prob = (count(prev, word) + alpha) / (count(prev) + alpha * V), where count(prev) is how many bigrams start with prev and V is the vocabulary size.
3. Perplexity = exp(-average log prob) over every transition, including the final one into `</s>`.
4. To sample, walk the words in sorted order, adding up probabilities until the total passes `rng.random()`. Sorting keeps a seeded run reproducible.

</details>
